newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds rise after strong jobs report.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds rise after strong jobs report.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities gained strongly after poring over U.S. employment data Friday morning, fixed-income analysts said.
By late Friday afternoon, some 30-year discount coupons were up as much as 15/32, rising as Treasuries recovered from an early stumble.
"The mortgage market was directional based on Treasuries," said Garitt Kono, a senior portfolio manager at Dreyfus Corp.
Treasuries fell off sharply following the jobs report, which said 250,000 new jobs were created in August as the unemployment rate dipped to 5.1 percent from 5.3 percent.
But after dropping a full point in the long end, they quickly recovered into positive territory.
"This was a market of foreign buying and hedge-fund buying with some intermittent domestic buying," said Kono.
Activity in pass-throughs generally was light, with volatility keeping most investors sidelined, traders said.
"There hasn't been a lot of retail involvement today," one trader said. "The market reaction after the number was too jerky, so a lot of people didn't get involved in mortgages."
Late on Friday, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were up 9/32 at 100-03/32, yielding 113 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable FNMAs were up 9/32 at 100-03/32, and FHLMCs were up 4/32 at 100-00/32.
The ten-year Treasury note was up 13/32 to yield 7.11 percent late in the day.
